source.note: Control IDs, defaults, scope, timing, classification and build tags are unchanged from Edition 5; screen mappings and visual/native contracts are revised.

status_definition.exists: End-to-end functional path in both hosts on at least one Rev8-screen surface, with a live daemon contract and specified states; only minor visual deltas remain.
status_definition.partial: UI and/or backend exists, but at least one of: one host, generic Edition 5 control-center row rather than the specified Rev8 screen, route/shape mismatch, missing state, or placeholder.
status_definition.missing: No functional UI/backend path for the control contract.

methodology.evidence: Catalog rows are exact line references in the current working tree. Implementation evidence is the nearest audited seam from the Edition 5 scan plus a matched native route. It proves the feature area exists; it does not prove Rev8 pixel/state acceptance.
methodology.screen_mapping: Every control-to-screen edge is parsed from the CONTROLS footer of the 72 design plates (pp.20-180). Screen design/contract page pairs are recorded per screen.
methodology.acceptance_mapping: A ids are derived by topic; the PDF does not provide a control-to-A crosswalk.
methodology.wave_assignment: Reconstructed from pp.225-226; not normative per control.
methodology.inspection_scope: Working-tree inspection at 2026-10-17/18 of apps/vscode/**, apps/jetbrains/frontend/** and backend, crates/cli/src/config/*, and crates/server/src/api/lifecycle.rs. Evidence lines are exact for catalog rows and matched routes; edition5 audit lines are retained where the file/symbol still exists.

ambiguities: The PDF states that all 200 controls have a Build_Map.csv row and that 838 copy changes are recorded, but the PDF itself does not include Build_Map.csv or the per-change ledger; build-map.csv and this artifact reconstruct the rows from the control contracts and plates.
The PDF gives global loading/stale/pending rules but does not provide separate copy for every control; per-control empty/error/disabled copy is the catalog text.
Host applicability is "both" for all 200 controls in the contract catalog; host-native surfaces differ per screen and are recorded per screen, not per control.
Actual route names are implementation evidence, not normative spec endpoints; the PDF explicitly says its backend names describe capabilities, not existing routes (p.226).
Some statuses are conservative: a control that is rendered only in the Edition 5 Control Center is partial even when a backend route exists.
